simple: the real flight program flies a pretend drone inside a computer.
analogy: Leila rehearsing her real walk in an empty hall while Tomás narrates the bumps.
precise: a test arrangement in which the flight software, compiled for a desktop or server computer, runs in a closed loop with a simulator that models the vehicle, its sensors, its actuators and its environment; the flight software's hardware drivers are replaced by an interface to the simulator. PX4 and ArduPilot both document SITL for their flight stacks.
source: D1 of F10-33 (PX4 Autopilot User Guide (PX4 project, Dronecode Foundation; tier 2): sections on simulation (software in the loop, the simulators it supports, lockstep simulation) and the architecture overview. Title only — not opened during this build; the Source Researcher must confirm the release and section titles (dossier gate G1 open).); D2 of F10-33 (ArduPilot documentation (ArduPilot project; tier 2): developer documentation on SITL and the simulated hardware layer. Title only — not opened during this build (dossier gate G1 open).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the program that pretends to be the drone, the air, the sensors and the radio.
analogy: Tomás and everything he describes.
precise: software that integrates a model of the vehicle's dynamics and produces synthetic sensor data (with modelled noise and faults) from the true simulated state, and that applies the flight software's actuator commands to the model; its fidelity is whatever its authors modelled, nothing more.
source: D3 of F10-33 (Randal W. Beard, Timothy W. McLain, "Small Unmanned Aircraft: Theory and Practice" (tier 3): vehicle and sensor models for simulation, and what a simplified model leaves out. Title only — not opened during this build; edition and chapters to be confirmed (dossier gate G1 open).); R1 of F10-33 (R1 — lab run of Listing 2 (sitl_mission.log): g++ 13.3.0 with AddressSanitizer and UBSan, exit code 0, deterministic.)

simple: the pretend world waits for the flight program's answer before it moves on.
analogy: Tomás waits until Leila has reacted before narrating the next moment.
precise: a scheme in which simulated time advances by one step only after the flight software has consumed that step's sensor data and returned its commands, so that the result does not depend on how fast either program runs on the host; PX4's documentation describes a lockstep mode of its simulation.
source: D1 of F10-33 (PX4 Autopilot User Guide (PX4 project, Dronecode Foundation; tier 2): sections on simulation (software in the loop, the simulators it supports, lockstep simulation) and the architecture overview. Title only — not opened during this build; the Source Researcher must confirm the release and section titles (dossier gate G1 open).); R1 of F10-33 (R1 — lab run of Listing 2 (sitl_mission.log): g++ 13.3.0 with AddressSanitizer and UBSan, exit code 0, deterministic.)

simple: the pretend world moves on with the clock, whether or not the flight program has answered.
analogy: Tomás talking at his own speed.
precise: a simulation whose time follows the host's wall clock (or a fixed multiple of it); when the host is busy, the flight software misses steps and the simulated vehicle flies on stale commands, so results depend on host load.
source: R2 of F10-33 (R2 — lab run of Listing 3 (lockstep.log): same toolchain, exit code 0; the free-running rows model host load with a seeded generator.)

simple: a written pass/fail rule checked automatically after a simulated flight.
analogy: "no water spilled and the tray reached the table".
precise: a predicate over the simulated flight's record (events, trajectory, energy) with a stated tolerance, for example "landing point within 1.5 m of home"; the tolerance must exceed the error the design itself allows, or the test fails without a defect.
source: R1 of F10-33 (R1 — lab run of Listing 2 (sitl_mission.log): g++ 13.3.0 with AddressSanitizer and UBSan, exit code 0, deterministic.)

simple: a test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails with no change to the code.
analogy: the rehearsal that spills on some walks because of Tomás's timing, not Leila's hands.
precise: a test whose verdict depends on uncontrolled inputs (host timing, unseeded randomness, test order, wall-clock reads) or whose tolerance sits inside the system's normal variation; it destroys trust in the suite and must be fixed, not re-run.
source: R3 of F10-33 (R3 — forensic evidence run (ci_flaky.log): same toolchain, exit code 0.)

simple: how far off a correct system can normally be, added up from every allowed source of error, so a test knows what "too far" means.
analogy: how far from the table Leila may stop and still be on target, given how wide the table is and how much the floor wobbles.
precise: the sum (or a stated combination) of the deviations a correct design is allowed to produce for a metric (for a landing point: acceptance radius, estimator noise, wind drift during descent); a test tolerance must lie outside this budget with a stated margin, or the test fails on correct code.
source: R1 of F10-33 (R1 — lab run of Listing 2 (sitl_mission.log): g++ 13.3.0 with AddressSanitizer and UBSan, exit code 0, deterministic.); R3 of F10-33 (R3 — forensic evidence run (ci_flaky.log): same toolchain, exit code 0.)

simple: the real flight-controller board runs the flight program, while a computer next to it pretends to be the world.
analogy: Leila with the real tray and shoes, while Tomás narrates over the phone.
precise: a test arrangement in which the flight software runs on the target flight controller (its processor, RTOS, memory and build), its sensor inputs are replaced by simulated data sent from a host simulator over a communication link, and its actuator outputs are sent back to the simulator instead of (or as well as) to the motors; PX4's documentation describes a HITL mode of this kind.
source: D1 of F10-34 (PX4 Autopilot User Guide (PX4 project, Dronecode Foundation; tier 2): "Hardware in the Loop Simulation" and the simulation overview. Title only — not opened during this build; release and section titles to be confirmed (dossier gate G1 open).); D2 of F10-34 (MAVLink Developer Guide (MAVLink project, Dronecode Foundation; tier 2): message framing and the message set used for simulation input and output. Title only — not opened during this build (dossier gate G1 open).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the cable and the message format that carry pretend sensor data to the board and motor commands back.
analogy: the phone line between Tomás and Leila.
precise: the physical connection (USB, a serial port, a network) plus the framing protocol that carries simulated sensor messages to the flight controller and actuator messages to the simulator; its capacity, latency, jitter and error behaviour become part of the control loop.
source: D2 of F10-34 (MAVLink Developer Guide (MAVLink project, Dronecode Foundation; tier 2): message framing and the message set used for simulation input and output. Title only — not opened during this build (dossier gate G1 open).); R1 of F10-34 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (hitl_link.log): g++ 13.3.0 with AddressSanitizer and UBSan, exit code 0.)

simple: a calculation of whether all the messages fit through the cable in time.
analogy: whether Tomás can say everything that happens before the next thing happens.
precise: the comparison of offered load (bytes per frame × frames per second, plus framing overhead such as start and stop bits) with the link's capacity; utilisation ρ = offered / capacity must stay well below 1, because when ρ > 1 the queue, and with it the age of the data, grows without bound.
source: C2 of F10-34 (University chapter F9-14 (RB201) and its sources: UART framing (start, data, parity, stop bits) and serial links. Cross-reference within this university; the claims are tagged there.); R3 of F10-34 (R3 — forensic evidence run (hitl_forensic.log): same toolchain, exit code 0; link and host modelled by the course program.)

simple: how old the newest sensor data on the board is.
analogy: how long ago the bump happened that Tomás is describing now.
precise: current time minus the simulated time stamp of the newest complete sensor frame the flight software has received; in HITL it adds directly to the loop's delay.
source: R3 of F10-34 (R3 — forensic evidence run (hitl_forensic.log): same toolchain, exit code 0; link and host modelled by the course program.)

simple: the order of rehearsals, each making one more part real.
analogy: plastic cups, then the real tray, then real drinks in an empty hall, then the party.
precise: the sequence SITL → HITL → bench tests with real sensors and actuators and propellers removed → restrained or tethered tests where available → supervised flight, each stage entered only when the previous one passed its acceptance tests; MP7's milestones follow it.
source: C1 of F10-34 (University Authoring Guide (local file): course card DN401, mega project MP7 (milestones, gates), bridge BR-08, faculty F10 safety rules. A map, not a source (AH-4).)

simple: what the drone does on its own when something important goes wrong.
analogy: "go back to the meeting point".
precise: the flight mode or behaviour (hold position, return to launch, land where it is, continue, or terminate) that the flight software switches to when a failsafe monitor detects its condition; flight stacks let the operator choose the action per failsafe, within limits.
source: D1 of F10-35 (PX4 Autopilot User Guide (PX4 project, Dronecode Foundation; tier 2): safety and failsafe configuration, battery estimation, geofence. Title only — not opened during this build (dossier gate G1 open).); D2 of F10-35 (ArduPilot documentation (ArduPilot project; tier 2): failsafe pages for multicopters (radio, battery, geofence). Title only — not opened during this build (dossier gate G1 open).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: when several problems happen, the drone only moves to safer and safer actions, never back.
analogy: once Leila has put the tray down, she does not pick it up again because the music started.
precise: an ordering of failsafe actions (in this course: continue < hold < return < land) with the rule that a new failsafe may switch to an action of higher rank but never to a lower one, so that a second fault cannot undo the response to a more serious first one.
source: R1 of F10-35 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (failsafe_matrix.log): g++ 13.3.0 with AddressSanitizer and UBSan, exit code 0, 0 of 7 cases failed.)

simple: rules that start the way home when the battery gets low, and land at once when it gets very low.
analogy: starting back to the kitchen while your arms still can, and putting the tray down if they start to shake.
precise: monitors on the estimated remaining charge (integrated current against a configured capacity) and/or on the loaded cell voltage, each with a threshold, a persistence time and an action; usually a "low" level that returns and a "critical" level that lands.
source: D1 of F10-35 (PX4 Autopilot User Guide (PX4 project, Dronecode Foundation; tier 2): safety and failsafe configuration, battery estimation, geofence. Title only — not opened during this build (dossier gate G1 open).); R1 of F10-35 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (failsafe_matrix.log): g++ 13.3.0 with AddressSanitizer and UBSan, exit code 0, 0 of 7 cases failed.)

simple: an invisible boundary the drone is not allowed to cross.
analogy: the red rope in front of the garden.
precise: a volume defined in the flight software (in this course a maximum horizontal distance from home and a maximum altitude; in flight stacks also polygons and inclusion and exclusion zones) whose breach, by the estimated position, triggers a configured action. A geofence acts on the estimate: a wrong position estimate makes the fence wrong too.
source: D1 of F10-35 (PX4 Autopilot User Guide (PX4 project, Dronecode Foundation; tier 2): safety and failsafe configuration, battery estimation, geofence. Title only — not opened during this build (dossier gate G1 open).); D2 of F10-35 (ArduPilot documentation (ArduPilot project; tier 2): failsafe pages for multicopters (radio, battery, geofence). Title only — not opened during this build (dossier gate G1 open).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: breaking something on purpose in a test to see whether the safety rule reacts.
analogy: the head waiter hiding on purpose during the rehearsal, to see whether Leila goes back to the meeting point.
precise: a test that introduces a specified fault (signal loss, a battery state, a position) at a specified time and checks the system's response against a written expectation: which action, within which deadline, and which end state.
source: R1 of F10-35 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (failsafe_matrix.log): g++ 13.3.0 with AddressSanitizer and UBSan, exit code 0, 0 of 7 cases failed.)

simple: what the radio receiver tells the flight controller when it stops hearing the transmitter.
analogy: the frozen hand sign of a head waiter who fell asleep.
precise: the receiver's configured behaviour when the RC link is lost: stop sending output, send a flagged failsafe state, or keep sending values (the last ones or preset ones); if the receiver keeps sending ordinary-looking values, the flight controller may not detect the loss at all.
source: R2 of F10-35 (R2 — forensic evidence run (rc_forensic.log): same toolchain, exit code 0; receiver model is the course program's.)

simple: a written explanation of why a planned flight is safe enough, with proof for each point.
analogy: Leila's sheet for the head waiter.
precise: a structured argument, supported by evidence, that a specific operation (vehicle, firmware and configuration, site, procedure, people) is acceptably safe; it lists the hazards, the mitigations and the evidence that each mitigation works, and it is valid only for the configuration and conditions it names. SS402 treats safety cases in general (F11-18).
source: D2 of F10-36 (GSN Community Standard. Title only — not opened during this build; not in the guide's source registry, proposed for addition in NOTES (dossier gate G1 open).); D3 of F10-36 (University chapters F11-18 and F11-19 (SS402) and their sources: hazard, risk, hazard analysis. Cross-reference within this university; claims are tagged there.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a way of drawing a safety argument as a tree of claims, ways of arguing, and proof.
analogy: each line on Leila's sheet split into smaller lines until each ends in "I know because…".
precise: a graphical notation for arguments with element types including goals (claims), strategies (how a goal is broken down), solutions (evidence), context and assumptions, and a marking for undeveloped goals, described in the GSN Community Standard; this course uses a small text format with goals, strategies and evidence only.
source: D2 of F10-36 (GSN Community Standard. Title only — not opened during this build; not in the guide's source registry, proposed for addition in NOTES (dossier gate G1 open).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a table that scores each danger by how bad it would be and how likely it is.
analogy: a spilled drink on the floor (minor, likely) against a tray falling on a child (severe, unlikely).
precise: a scheme that assigns each hazard a severity class and a likelihood class on ordinal scales and combines them (in this course as the product of two 1–5 scores) to compare risk before and after mitigation against an acceptance limit fixed in advance; the scores are judgements to be justified, not measurements, and the product of ordinal scores is a ranking aid, not a probability.
source: D3 of F10-36 (University chapters F11-18 and F11-19 (SS402) and their sources: hazard, risk, hazard analysis. Cross-reference within this university; claims are tagged there.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: proof only counts if it was made with the same software and settings that will fly.
analogy: Leila practised in her old shoes, then bought new ones: the practice says little about the new shoes.
precise: the property that each item of evidence was produced with the firmware build and configuration identifier named by the safety case; a change of either invalidates evidence until the affected tests are repeated or an impact analysis argues that they still hold.
source: R1 of F10-36 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 on safety_case.in (safety_case.log): g++ 13.3.0 with AddressSanitizer and UBSan, exit code 0.)

simple: a written question about the rules, with the answer and exactly where the answer was read.
analogy: "may I serve in the garden?" with "no, house rules page 2, read on Monday".
precise: an entry in the lab sheet that states one question about the rules for a flight, the answer, the official document it comes from (authority, title, edition), and the date read; answers without an official source are not accepted.
source: D1 of F10-36 (The national aviation authority's current rules for unmanned aircraft where the learner lives (tier 1; per learner, recorded in the lab sheet). Not opened during this build: the learner reads them; this chapter states no rule content.); C1 of F10-36 (University Authoring Guide (local file): safety rules for drone flights, source tiers (tier 6 never used), DN401 course card, MP7 gates. A map, not a source (AH-4).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the written plan for a test flight: who does what, in what order, and when to stop.
analogy: the head waiter's plan for the evening, from the kitchen door to clearing the tables.
precise: a document that defines the test's objective, the roles and their authority, the phases (preparation, set-up, pre-flight, flight cards, post-flight), the abort criteria and the abort actions, and the records to be produced; it implements the procedure claims of the safety case.
source: C1 of F10-37 (University Authoring Guide (local file): DN401 course card (lab, exam P), MP7 gate R3 checks, F10 safety rules. A map, not a source (AH-4).); D2 of F10-37 (Atul Gawande, "The Checklist Manifesto". Title only — not opened during this build; not in the guide's source registry, proposed in NOTES (dossier gate G1 open).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list of things that must all be true before the drone may fly, each signed.
analogy: the three-second look at the kitchen door.
precise: a list of checkable items, each with a category that sets how fresh the check must be, a status, a time, the name of the person who checked it, and a grade (stop item or note); the decision is GO only if every stop item is satisfied and fresh, the vehicle matches the record, the roles are filled and the supervisor has signed.
source: D1 of F10-37 (University chapter F0-46 (KID103) and its glossary entry checklist. Cross-reference within this university.); R1 of F10-37 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 on gonogo.in (gonogo.log): g++ 13.3.0 with AddressSanitizer and UBSan, exit code 0.)

simple: how long a check stays valid before it must be done again.
analogy: yesterday's check was for yesterday's tray.
precise: the maximum age of a check at the start of the test, set per category (in this course: documents a year, day items 12 h, field items 60 min); a check older than its limit counts as not done.
source: R1 of F10-37 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 on gonogo.in (gonogo.log): g++ 13.3.0 with AddressSanitizer and UBSan, exit code 0.)

simple: a condition, agreed before the flight, that ends it at once.
analogy: "if a child runs into your path, stop and hold the tray high", agreed before the party.
precise: an observable condition (a person entering the exclusion zone, loss of visual contact, unexpected behaviour, a failsafe, a limit exceeded) with a defined call, a defined action (land, return, or cut motors under the conditions the procedure allows), and the person entitled to call it, normally anyone on the team.
source: C1 of F10-37 (University Authoring Guide (local file): DN401 course card (lab, exam P), MP7 gate R3 checks, F10 safety rules. A map, not a source (AH-4).)

simple: one short card per flight that says exactly what this flight will do.
analogy: "this trip: three glasses to table 4, then back".
precise: a one-page plan for a single flight: objective, manoeuvres in order, mode for each, height and area, expected duration and battery, abort criteria specific to this flight, and the data to record; flown as written, changed only on the ground.
source: C1 of F10-37 (University Authoring Guide (local file): DN401 course card (lab, exam P), MP7 gate R3 checks, F10 safety rules. A map, not a source (AH-4).)

simple: the recording that a drone's flight computer makes of what it measured, decided and commanded during a flight.
analogy: the stains on the floor and the guests' notes.
precise: a time-stamped record written by the flight software (sensor values, estimates, setpoints, commands, modes, events, parameters, versions) at defined rates; flight stacks have their own formats (PX4 writes ULog files, F10-25; ArduPilot writes its own binary logs), and the course uses a CSV format with comment lines. A log contains only what the software knew, never the truth.
source: D1 of F10-38 (PX4 Autopilot User Guide (PX4 project, Dronecode Foundation; tier 2): flight log analysis, ULog, logging. Title only — not opened during this build (dossier gate G1 open).); D2 of F10-38 (ArduPilot documentation (ArduPilot project; tier 2): logs and log analysis for multicopters. Title only — not opened during this build (dossier gate G1 open).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a drone flying off in a direction nobody commanded, and not coming back under control.
analogy: Leila's circles growing until she reaches the rope.
precise: loss of position control in which the vehicle departs from its intended position or path in an uncommanded way; causes include a wrong heading or position estimate, a configuration error, and loss of control authority.
source: R2 of F10-38 (R2 — lab runs of gen_logs, Listing 1 and Listing 3 on Log A (gen_logs.log, logscan.log, show_rows.log): same toolchain, exit code 0; logs generated by the course simulator.)

simple: magnetic fields from the drone's own power wires that fool its compass, more when the motors work harder.
analogy: a magnet in Leila's pocket that pulls a compass needle more the faster she walks.
precise: a disturbance of the magnetometer reading by the magnetic field of currents in the vehicle's power wiring, proportional to the current and fixed in the body frame; it is absent on the ground with motors stopped, so a ground calibration and pre-arm checks do not see it, and it rotates the heading estimate in flight.
source: D3 of F10-38 (Magnetometer and GNSS/compass module datasheets and installation guides of the course kit (tier 1; recorded per kit), and university chapter F10-08 (DN202) on sensors. Not opened during this build; the interference model in the logs is the course simulator's.); R2 of F10-38 (R2 — lab runs of gen_logs, Listing 1 and Listing 3 on Log A (gen_logs.log, logscan.log, show_rows.log): same toolchain, exit code 0; logs generated by the course simulator.)

simple: a drone circling around the point it is trying to hold, in growing or steady loops.
analogy: water circling in a bowl.
precise: a circular oscillation of a position loop caused by a heading error: each correction is rotated by the error, so it pushes partly sideways; above a critical error the loop is unstable and, with acceleration and speed limits, settles into circles that may grow. The informal name is common in drone communities; the course uses it with this definition.
source: R1 of F10-38 (R1 — lab run of Listing 2 (heading_margin.log): g++ 13.3.0 with AddressSanitizer and UBSan, exit code 0.)

simple: the deepest reason something went wrong, and the other things that made it worse or let it through.
analogy: the slippery floor (root cause), and the missing rope and the new shoes (contributing).
precise: the root cause is the fault whose removal would have prevented the incident; contributing factors are conditions that made it possible, worse or undetected (process gaps, missing checks, configuration). A blameless analysis looks for both and asks which defence failed, not who.
source: C1 of F10-38 (University Authoring Guide (local file): DN401 course card (forensic: two logs, full written analysis), MP7 deliverables, blameless post-mortems at L5. A map, not a source (AH-4).)
